summary: A 1937 Aermotor fire tower with a raised-platform cab on Bill Williams Mountain above Williams, Arizona; the register lists it in active service.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-39 tower with a 7' x 7' metal cab and a raised platform above the roof
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kaibab National Forest (Williams Ranger District)

access.note: Open to visitors during fire season according to an undated Arizona Highways article. Current opening not confirmed. The summit road serves radio towers.

visit.trail_note: Trail starts at the Williams Ranger District station about a mile from downtown Williams. The route crosses Forest Road 111, which serves the radio towers on the summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1937 date is for the present Aermotor tower. A patrol lookout (1910) and a 30-foot wooden tower (1924) stood on the summit before it.

notes_for_editor: Current staffing and whether the lookout is open this season are unknown. The only opening statement is an undated Arizona Highways article. The record's height_m 13.7 (sourced to Wikidata) is not supported by any source I read, so it is not in facts. Summit elevation conflicts: the register gives 9,166 ft (matches the record) while 1935 and 1939 newspapers give 9,264 and 9,242 ft; a paywalled Trails Offroad listing gives 9,227 ft and was not used. The 2014 Forest Service project concerns the summit radio tower, not the lookout. No new photos found.
